seo.title: Free Temporary Chat Room – No Sign-Up, Private P2P Chat | CuisineChat
seo.description: Create a private chat room in seconds: pick a room ID, share a 3-digit code and chat peer-to-peer with photos, files and voice messages. No sign-up, nothing stored on servers.
seo.keywords: temporary chat room, anonymous chat room, private chat room, chat room no sign up, online chat room with password, P2P chat, encrypted chat, disposable chat, send files online
seo.imageAlt: CuisineChat: a glowing lantern beside a chat preview. One room ID plus a 3-digit code; chat, share, then it vanishes.

landing.what: CuisineChat is a free, temporary chat room that runs entirely in your web browser. Two or more people open the same room by typing the same room ID and a 3-digit code, then exchange text, photos, files and voice messages directly over peer-to-peer WebRTC connections. There is no sign-up and no server-side message storage: by default the conversation is gone once you close the page, or you can choose to keep it on your own device for 1 to 27 hours.
landing.how1: Type any name, or tap “Create Room” to get a random one.
landing.how2: Friends who enter the same room ID and code join the same room.
landing.how3: Messages travel directly between browsers. By default they disappear when you close the page; you can choose to keep them on your device for 1–27 hours.
landing.f1: No account, email or phone number. You get a random food nickname like Ramen or Tiramisu.
landing.f2: Messages, photos and files go straight between devices over encrypted WebRTC connections.
landing.f3: There is no database. History stays in your browser — optionally saved on your own device for 1–27 hours, then deleted automatically.
landing.f4: Share images, files up to 20 MB and voice messages in the same room.
landing.f5: Runs in any modern browser on phone or desktop — nothing to install.
landing.f6: Available in English, 中文, 日本語 and 한국어.
landing.a1: Yes. There is no sign-up and no paid plan.
landing.a2: Never on a server. By default messages are gone once you close the page. If you turn on “Chat history” in Settings, they are kept only in your own browser for the 1–27 hours you choose, then deleted automatically.
landing.a3: Data travels over WebRTC, which encrypts every connection (DTLS). A public signaling server only helps browsers find each other and never sees your messages.
landing.q4: How many people can join a room?
landing.a4: Small groups work best, because every participant connects directly to everyone else.
landing.a5: Make sure you both use exactly the same room ID and 3-digit code. Strict company or school networks can block peer-to-peer connections.
